facts.text: Tyler’s Danebod district, built by Danish settlers, opened its folk school in 1888 and now sits on the National Register of Historic Places.
The Danebod Lutheran Church campus, part of the historic district, has been listed on the National Register since 1975 for its architectural and historic value.
Tyler was platted in 1879, and a post office has operated there continuously since that same year.
The town’s name honors Tyler, a Minnesota land agent and newspaper editor who helped shape the region’s early development.
If you’re curious before you arrive, the Tyler Library welcomes visitors, and the nearby park offers a reading adventure for book lovers.
Tyler’s southern edge hosts the Danebod historic district, where the campus of the Danebod Lutheran Church stands as a testament to Danish heritage.
